svg.title: Classification and Coverage Around the Owner
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-classification-and-coverage-map; chapter number: 11; chart type: org_architecture; title: Classification and Coverage Around the Owner; subtitle: Decided by control, not by the label or the form; caption: Operators, accountants and insurance agents converge on control as the test for W2 versus 1099, and price bonds, general liability and workers comp before bidding.; assumptions note: Premiums and rates are quotes reported at the time of filming; New York comp rates are 2022 base rates for class codes 9026, 9027 and 9028.; note: Sources Commercial Cleaning CEO (9BXhBVRp_XU at 00:03:59); Surety Bonds Direct (uMW_ZJMW0ZU at 00:04:12); The Janitorial Store (YC2NrvVJqlg at 00:03:13); The Professional Cleaner (DDLzG49aDvU at 00:03:20); The Coyle Group (HSh0vcHYmUI at 00:00:56).; center: role: Owner as classification gatekeeper; headcount: 10 employees in the Surety Bonds Direct commercial bond example; focus: Control decides status; settle classification with an accountant before the first helper starts.; spokes: role: W2 cleaning crew; type: Employee; kpi: Bonded at $328 a year for a $50,000 bond with 10 employees; role: 1099 subcontractor; type: Independent contractor; kpi: Has clients other than you; no schedules, supplies, uniforms or how-to instructions from you; role: General liability carrier; type: Insurance; kpi: $1,000,000 aggregate and $500,000 per occurrence at $30-$100 a month; role: Workers comp carrier; type: Insurance; kpi: New York 2022 base rates $12.31 down to $3.03 per class code
